newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen kidnappers seize five German tourists.
newsitem.headline: Yemen kidnappers seize five German tourists.

text.p: Yemeni kidnappers on Wednesday seized five German tourists in the southeastern province of Hadramaut, a Yemeni security source said.

"The kidnappers, who did not identify themselves, telephoned local authorities and asked them for a 12 million mark ($7 million) ransom to release them," he told Reuters without giving further details.
A German embassy official said: "We have nothing on the matter."
Yemeni tribes with grievances against the government or foreign oil companies have kidnapped scores of tourists, diplomats or other foreigners in recent years to use as bargaining chips.
An American diplomat and the Saudi ambassador have been among the kidnap victims. There have been no reported casualties from the abductions and all of the hostages have been released unharmed.
Some were rescued by security forces, others were set free.
An American oil engineer kidnapped by a Yemeni mountain tribes was released on February 26 after being held for 16 days.

His kidnappers had demanded compensation of $2 million or the return of a piece of land in Sanaa which they said was given to one of their tribal leaders. It was not clear whether their demands had been met in return for the engineer's release.
